states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and you hand back possession of the home
states.deadline_note: Give your landlord a forwarding address in writing when you move out; without one, the landlord mails to your last known address. A refund or check you don't claim within 90 days is forfeited.
states.itemization: If the landlord keeps any of the deposit, they must give you an itemized list of the amounts withheld within the same 60 days. Mailing it first class to the address you gave counts.
states.penalty: If the landlord does not mail the refund or the itemized list within 60 days, the landlord owes you double the amount of your original deposit. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.source_quote: If the landlord fails to mail a timely refund or accounting within the 60-day period, the landlord shall pay the tenant double the amount of the tenant’s original deposit.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not mail the refund or the itemized list within 60 days owes the tenant double the original deposit

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and you hand back possession of the home
states.deadline_note: The landlord has 14 days if you gave proper move-out notice and nothing is deducted for damage. The landlord gets 30 days if they deduct for damage, or if you did not give proper notice (then the clock can also start when the landlord learns the unit was abandoned).
states.itemization: A written notice, mailed to your last known address, listing any unpaid rent and damage charges taken from the deposit, together with the refund owed to you.
states.penalty: If the landlord willfully (on purpose) fails to follow the rule, you can recover up to twice the amount withheld.
states.source_quote: the landlord shall mail the written notice and refund required by (b) of this section within 14 days after the tenancy is terminated and possession is delivered by the tenant
states.flag: Two deadlines: 14 days or 30 days, depending on whether the landlord deducts for damage and whether you gave proper written move-out notice. The 14-day deadline still applies if the only deduction is unpaid rent and you gave proper notice. The deposit rules also do not cover everything for units renting above $2,000 a month (the deposit cap does not apply to those).
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who willfully fails to follow these rules can be ordered to pay the tenant up to twice the amount withheld

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends, you hand back possession, and you ask the landlord for the deposit
states.deadline_note: Weekends and legal holidays are not counted. The clock needs a demand from you, so ask for your deposit in writing when you move out. You have 60 days after the list is mailed to dispute the deductions, or you lose the right to.
states.itemization: An itemized list of all deductions together with any money owed to you, sent by first class mail to your last known address unless you arranged something else in writing.
states.penalty: You can recover the money owed to you plus damages equal to twice the amount wrongfully withheld. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.source_quote: Within fourteen days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays or other legal holidays, after termination of the tenancy and delivery of possession and demand by the tenant the landlord shall provide the tenant an itemized list of all deductions
states.flag: The 14 days are business days and only start once you have moved out AND demanded the deposit back. If you do not dispute the landlord's list within 60 days of mailing, the landlord's numbers become final. Mobile home park lot rentals are covered by a different law.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover the money owed plus damages equal to twice the amount wrongfully withheld

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and you hand back possession of the home
states.deadline_note: The landlord complies by mailing the list and payment first class to your last known address. If the payment comes back undelivered and the landlord cannot find you, it becomes the landlord's after 180 days.
states.itemization: A written notice itemizing any unpaid rent and damage charges taken from the deposit, delivered with the rest of the money owed to you.
states.penalty: You can recover the money owed, plus damages of 2 times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees. The landlord owes only the amount withheld and costs if they prove it was an honest mistake or a good-faith dispute over the amount.
states.source_quote: Within sixty (60) days of termination of the tenancy, property or money held by the landlord as security shall be returned to the tenant.
states.flag: These rules do not cover small landlords: an individual who owns 5 or fewer rental units is exempt, unless a paid manager runs the unit or collects the rent. We could not open the official state code online, so this was checked against a free copy of the 2025 code (Justia) instead. Confirm it before relying on it.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover the money owed plus damages of twice the amount wrongfully withheld, along with court costs and reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out
states.deadline_note: Give the landlord an address; otherwise mail goes to the unit you left. If repairs can't be finished or bills aren't in within 21 days, the landlord may deduct a good-faith estimate and must send the final paperwork within 14 days of finishing.
states.itemization: An itemized statement of deductions with the refund. If repair and cleaning deductions total more than $125, the landlord must include receipts or invoices (or a description of work, time and hourly rate if done in-house) and before-and-after photos.
states.penalty: If the landlord keeps the deposit in bad faith, a court can award up to twice the amount of the deposit on top of your actual losses. A landlord who in bad faith ignores the itemization rules cannot keep any of the deposit.
states.interest: None required by state law (some cities, such as Los Angeles and San Francisco, require it by local ordinance)
states.source_quote: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises ... the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement
states.flag: The penalty of up to twice the deposit requires bad faith and is up to the judge. Your city may add its own rules, such as interest on deposits.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith can be ordered to pay up to twice the amount of the deposit, in addition to the tenant's actual losses

states.deadline_trigger: after the lease ends or you move out and hand back the home, whichever is later
states.deadline_note: The lease can set a longer deadline, but never more than 60 days, so check your lease. The landlord can send the statement to your last known address or an email address they have for you.
states.itemization: A written statement listing the exact reasons for keeping any part of the deposit, sent with the rest of your money. If you ask in writing, the landlord has 14 days to give you photos, inspection reports, receipts, invoices or estimates supporting the deductions.
states.penalty: A landlord who misses the deadline or wrongfully keeps money loses the right to keep any of the deposit and owes 3 times the amount wrongfully withheld plus attorney fees and court costs. You must first send a demand and 7 days' notice that you plan to sue; triple damages apply only if the landlord still does not pay within those 7 days.
states.citation: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-103 (as amended by HB25-1249, effective Jan. 1, 2026)
states.source_quote: A landlord shall, within thirty days after the termination of a lease or surrender of a premises, whichever occurs last, return to the tenant the full security deposit deposited with the landlord by the tenant
states.flag: Check your lease: it can extend the deadline from 30 days to as many as 60. To get triple damages you must first send a written demand and 7 days' notice that you plan to sue. The law changed on January 1, 2026, and many websites still show the old wording. We checked the 2026 law as passed, not the compiled statute book.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who wrongfully keeps a deposit can owe three times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus attorney fees and court costs, if it is not paid within 7 days of the tenant's written notice of intent to sue. Please treat this letter as that notice

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: The deadline is 21 days after the tenancy ends or 15 days after the landlord gets your forwarding address in writing, whichever is later. Send your forwarding address in writing right away.
states.itemization: Either the full deposit plus interest, or the balance plus a written statement itemizing the nature and amount of each damage charge.
states.penalty: A landlord who breaks the rule owes twice the amount of the security deposit. If the only violation is not paying the interest, the landlord owes $10 or twice the interest, whichever is more. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.interest: Yes. Landlords must pay yearly interest at a rate at least equal to the state 'deposit index' set each year by the Banking Commissioner; unpaid interest is due within 21 days after the tenancy ends. No interest for any month rent was more than 10 days late, unless a late fee was charged.
states.source_quote: Not later than twenty-one days after termination of a tenancy or fifteen days after receiving written notification of such tenant's forwarding address, whichever is later
states.flag: The clock does not finish until 15 days after the landlord receives your forwarding address in writing. The deadline was shortened from 30 to 21 days by a 2023 law (P.A. 23-207), so older guides are out of date.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not follow these rules is liable for twice the amount of the security deposit

states.deadline_trigger: after the rental agreement ends
states.deadline_note: Give the landlord a forwarding address in writing at or before the end of the lease; without it the landlord is not liable for the double penalty (you can still claim the unused deposit in writing within 1 year). If you cash a partial refund, object in writing within 10 days of receiving it or you are treated as agreeing to the deductions.
states.itemization: An itemized list of damage to the home with the estimated repair cost of each item, sent with payment of the difference.
states.penalty: If the landlord does not send the deposit (or the difference with the damage list) within 20 days, you are entitled to double the amount wrongfully withheld. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.source_quote: Within 20 days after the termination or expiration of any rental agreement, the landlord shall provide the tenant with an itemized list of damages to the premises and the estimated costs of repair for each
states.flag: Two traps for tenants: you must give a written forwarding address by the end of the lease to keep the double penalty, and you must object in writing within 10 days of receiving a partial refund or you are treated as accepting the landlord's deductions.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not return the deposit or send the itemized list on time owes the tenant double the amount wrongfully withheld

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: Within 45 days the landlord must either return the deposit with interest or tell you in writing that they intend to keep some of it. If they send that notice, they have 30 more days to refund the balance and send the itemized list.
states.itemization: An itemized statement of the repairs and other uses the money was applied to and the cost of each. A 2026 law also requires the 45-day notice of any amounts claimed to include photos or other documentation and tell you how to dispute it (you have 30 days).
states.penalty: If the landlord misses these steps, you are presumed entitled to the full deposit with interest. If the landlord kept it in bad faith, you can recover 3 times the amount.
states.interest: Yes. The deposit must be kept in an interest-bearing escrow account and interest is paid to you at the end of a tenancy that lasted 12 months or more.
states.source_quote: Within 45 days after termination of the tenancy, the housing provider shall notify the tenant in writing, either personally, by email, or by certified mail at the tenant's forwarding address, of any alleged unpaid amounts due
states.flag: Two-step process, so the full wait can be up to 75 days: 45 days to refund or tell you in writing they plan to keep some, then 30 more days for the itemized list and the balance. These rules are in city regulations (14 DCMR §§ 309-311). We could not open the official regulations site, so the deadline and the triple-damages rule were checked against unofficial copies only. Confirm them before relying on them.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who misses these steps is presumed to owe the full deposit with interest, and a landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith can owe three times the amount

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out at the end of the rental agreement
states.deadline_note: 15 days to return the full deposit if the landlord claims nothing; 30 days to send you a written notice if the landlord wants to keep any of it. If you leave early or are on a periodic tenancy and do not give 7 days' written notice with your new address, the landlord is excused from sending the notice.
states.itemization: A written notice, by certified mail to your last known address (or email if you agreed to email notices), stating the amount the landlord intends to claim and the reason. The statute does not require receipts or photos.
states.penalty: No multiplier. A landlord who misses the 30-day notice loses the right to keep any of the deposit and must return it all (but can still sue you separately for damages). Whoever wins a court case over the deposit gets court costs and attorney fees.
states.interest: Not required. Interest is owed only if the landlord chooses to keep the deposit in an interest-bearing account (at least 75% of the account's rate, or 5% a year) or posts a surety bond (5% a year).
states.source_quote: the landlord must, within 30 days after the termination of the rental agreement, provide the tenant written notice by certified mail to the tenant’s last known mailing address or by e-mail
states.flag: Special procedure: after the landlord's notice of claim, you have 15 days from receiving it to object in writing, or the landlord may deduct the claim and must send the balance within 30 days of the notice. Not objecting does not stop you suing later. If you lose in court you may have to pay the landlord's attorney fees. Skipping the required 7-day move-out notice can cost you the landlord's notice. Some public and federally subsidized housing is treated differently.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not send the required notice of claim within 30 days loses the right to keep any of the deposit, and the winning side in court can recover court costs and attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the landlord gets the unit back (the lease has ended and you have moved out, or the landlord has accepted your move-out)
states.deadline_note: The landlord meets the deadline by mailing the refund and statement by first-class mail to your last known address, so make sure the landlord has your new address. The landlord is also supposed to inspect and write up a damage list within 3 business days of move-out, and you can ask to inspect within 5 business days.
states.itemization: If the landlord keeps any of the deposit, they must send a written statement giving the exact reasons, including the full move-out damage list with estimated dollar amounts if the reason is damage, along with payment of the rest of the deposit.
states.penalty: Up to 3 times the amount wrongfully kept, plus reasonable attorney fees. The landlord owes only the amount wrongfully kept if they prove it was an honest mistake and not intentional. A landlord who misses the deadline for the lists and statement loses the right to keep anything for damage. These penalties do not apply to some small landlords (see warning).
states.source_quote: Within 30 days after obtaining possession of the premises as provided in subsection (b) of Code Section 44-7-33, a landlord shall return to the tenant the full security deposit
states.flag: Small-landlord exception: if the owner is an individual who owns 10 or fewer rental units and manages them personally, the 3-times penalty and the damage-list rules do not apply (the 30-day deadline still does). If you signed the landlord's move-out damage list without objecting in writing, you may lose the right to dispute those items. We could not open the official state code online, so this was checked against a free copy of the 2025 code (Justia) instead. Confirm it before relying on it.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who wrongfully keeps a deposit can owe up to three times the amount wrongfully kept, plus reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the rental agreement ends
states.deadline_note: The landlord meets the deadline if the refund or notice is mailed to an address you gave them and postmarked by midnight of the 14th day. You must file any court case to get the deposit back within one year after the rental agreement ends.
states.itemization: Written notice of what is being kept and why, with written proof of the costs such as estimates, invoices or receipts for repairs and cleaning.
states.penalty: If the landlord misses the 14-day deadline for the notice, they cannot keep any of the deposit. In small claims court you get back the amount wrongly kept plus court costs; if the landlord kept it wrongly and on purpose, the court may award 3 times that amount plus court costs.
states.source_quote: shall be returned to the tenant not later than fourteen days after the termination of the rental agreement.
states.flag: The 3-times award is only for deposits kept wrongly AND on purpose, and is up to the judge. Deposit disputes go to small claims court, where neither side may have a lawyer; if the court finds the landlord was entitled to keep the disputed amount, you can be ordered to pay the landlord's court costs. A tenant who leaves for 20 or more days without written notice and without paying rent can be treated as having abandoned the unit, and the landlord may keep the whole deposit.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who misses the 14-day deadline cannot keep any of the deposit, and a court may award three times the amount if it was wrongfully and willfully kept

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out and hand the unit back to the landlord
states.deadline_note: 21 days is the default. Your lease can set a different time, but never more than 30 days after you hand the unit back.
states.itemization: Any refund of less than the full deposit must come with a signed statement listing the amounts kept, the purpose of each, and a detailed list of what was spent from the deposit.
states.penalty: You can sue for the deposit, and the court may award up to 3 times your actual damages. Before suing you must give the landlord a written demand and wait 3 days. The deposit law itself does not set an automatic penalty.
states.source_quote: Refunds shall be made within twenty-one (21) days if no time is fixed by agreement and, in any event, within thirty (30) days after surrender of the premises by the tenant.
states.flag: The deadline depends on the lease: 21 days unless the lease sets another period, with a hard limit of 30 days. The 3-times award is at the judge's discretion, not automatic, and you must send a written 3-day demand before you can sue.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can sue for the deposit three days after a written demand, and the court may award up to three times the tenant's actual damages. Please treat this letter as that demand

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out or your right to live there ends, whichever is later
states.deadline_note: To keep money for damage, the landlord must send the itemized statement within 30 days. If no statement is sent, the full deposit is due within 45 days of the date you moved out. If the statement used estimated costs, paid receipts must follow within 30 more days. Give the landlord a mailing or email address; without one the landlord is not liable for penalties.
states.itemization: An itemized statement of the damage and the estimated or actual cost to fix each item, with paid receipts or copies attached (or, if receipts cannot be produced through no fault of the landlord, an itemized cost list and a sworn explanation). It can be delivered by hand, by mail, or by email to an address you provided.
states.penalty: Twice the amount of the deposit owed, plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees. This applies when a court finds the landlord refused to send the itemized statement or sent it in bad faith, and did not return the deposit owed on time.
states.interest: Required only where the building or complex has 25 or more units and the deposit is held more than 6 months; the rate is tied to a bank passbook savings rate and is paid yearly. Public housing is excluded. Smaller buildings: none required by state law.
states.citation: 765 ILCS 710/1 (Security Deposit Return Act); 765 ILCS 715/1-2 (Security Deposit Interest Act)
states.source_quote: within 30 days of the date that the lessee vacated the leased premises or within 30 days of the date the lessee's right of possession ends, whichever is later
states.flag: Rules vary by location. The 30 days is the deadline for an itemized statement of damage; if the landlord sends no statement, the full deposit is due within 45 days. State law does not spell out a deadline for deductions for unpaid rent. Since 2024 the state law covers all residential landlords (many websites still say only buildings with 5 or more units). Chicago, Evanston, Cook County and some other places have their own rules with different deadlines and penalties that may apply instead. We did not research those.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who refuses to send the itemized statement, or sends it in bad faith, and does not return the deposit on time can owe twice the amount of the deposit, plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the rental agreement ends and you move out and give the unit back
states.deadline_note: You must give the landlord your mailing address in writing; the landlord is not liable under this law until you do.
states.itemization: A mailed itemized list of the damage claimed, with the estimated repair cost for each item and the amounts the landlord intends to charge you, along with a check or money order for the rest of the deposit.
states.penalty: If the landlord does not send the itemized notice in time, they are treated as agreeing no damages are owed and must return the full deposit right away. You can recover the amount wrongly kept plus reasonable attorney fees and court costs. There is no multiplied penalty.
states.source_quote: Not more than forty-five (45) days after the termination of occupancy, a landlord shall mail to a tenant an itemized list of damages claimed for which the security deposit may be used
states.flag: The landlord's duty depends on you providing a mailing address in writing; until you do, the landlord is not liable under this law.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not send the itemized notice on time must return the full deposit and can owe the tenant's reasonable attorney fees and court costs

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and the landlord has received your mailing address or delivery instructions
states.deadline_note: The clock does not start until the landlord has your mailing address or delivery instructions. If you do not provide one within one year after the tenancy ends, the deposit goes to the landlord and you lose your right to it.
states.itemization: A written statement showing the specific reason for keeping any of the deposit; if money is kept to restore the unit, the statement must describe the damage.
states.penalty: A landlord who does not send the written statement within the 30 days loses the right to keep any of the deposit. If the landlord kept the deposit in bad faith, you can also get punitive damages of up to twice the monthly rent, on top of your actual damages. The court may award attorney fees to whoever wins.
states.interest: Not required. If the landlord keeps the deposit in an interest-bearing account, interest earned during the first five years of the tenancy belongs to the landlord.
states.source_quote: A landlord shall, within thirty days from the date of termination of the tenancy and receipt of the tenant's mailing address or delivery instructions, return the rental deposit to the tenant or furnish to the tenant a written statement
states.flag: The 30 days only start once the landlord has your mailing address or delivery instructions, and you lose the deposit entirely if you never provide one within a year. The extra penalty requires bad faith and is based on monthly rent (up to twice the monthly rent), not on the deposit amount. Attorney fees can be awarded to whichever side wins, including the landlord.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not send the written statement within 30 days loses the right to keep any of the deposit, and a landlord who keeps it in bad faith can owe punitive damages of up to twice the monthly rent

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends, you move out and hand back the unit, and you ask for the deposit back
states.deadline_note: If the landlord is keeping money for damage or other charges, the rest must be returned within 14 days after the landlord works out the amount, and never later than 30 days. If you do not ask for the deposit within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must mail what is owed to your last known address.
states.itemization: A written notice delivered to you that itemizes the unpaid rent and damages being taken out of the deposit.
states.penalty: The part of the deposit you are owed, plus damages equal to 1.5 times the amount wrongfully kept. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.source_quote: within 14 days after the determination of the amount of such expenses, damages or other charges, but in no event to exceed 30 days after termination of the tenancy, delivery of possession and demand by the tenant.
states.flag: The 30-day limit is tied to you asking for the deposit back (best done in writing), and a shorter 14-day clock runs from whenever the landlord works out the deductions, a date a renter usually cannot know. If you use the deposit as your last month's rent without the lease allowing it, you forfeit the deposit and still owe the rent.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover the part of the deposit owed plus damages equal to one and a half times the amount wrongfully kept

states.deadline_note: Kentucky's statute does not give a number of days for returning the deposit. It only says that if you owe no rent and are due a refund, the landlord must notify you at your last known address, and if you do not respond within 60 days the landlord may keep the money.
states.itemization: At move-out the landlord must inspect and write a full list of any damage being charged against the deposit, with the estimated repair cost. You have the right to inspect, and you must sign the list or state in writing which items you disagree with.
states.penalty: The statute provides no extra penalty or multiplier. A landlord cannot keep any of the deposit if it was not held in a separate bank account and the move-in and move-out damage lists were not provided. You can sue in District Court, but only over items you objected to in writing.
states.source_quote: In the event the landlord shall not have received a response from the tenant within sixty (60) days from the sending of such notification, the landlord may remove the deposit from the account
states.flag: No statewide deadline: the statute sets no number of days for returning a deposit (the quote shown is the 60-day rule for unclaimed refunds, not a return deadline). This section is part of Kentucky's landlord-tenant act, which by its terms (KRS 383.500) applies only in cities and counties that have adopted it, so it may not apply where you live; elsewhere the lease and general contract law control. If you do not sign the move-out damage list or object to specific items in writing, you cannot recover under this law. Respond quickly to any refund notice, because the landlord may keep the money after 60 days of silence.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord cannot keep any of the deposit unless it was held in a separate account and the required move-in and move-out damage lists were provided, and a tenant can sue to recover it

states.deadline_trigger: after the lease ends, as long as you gave proper notice and did not leave early
states.deadline_note: The law says "one month", not 30 days. Under a 2026 change, the landlord's itemized statement of deductions may be sent up to 15 days after that one-month mark. Give the landlord a forwarding address when the lease ends.
states.itemization: If any of the deposit is kept, an itemized statement accounting for the money kept and giving the reasons.
states.penalty: For a willful failure to follow the law, you can recover the amount wrongly kept plus $300 or twice the amount wrongly kept, whichever is greater. Not paying within 30 days after your written demand for a refund counts as willful. The court may award costs and attorney fees to whoever wins.
states.source_quote: shall be returned to the tenant or lessee of residential or dwelling premises within one month after the lease shall terminate.
states.flag: Recently changed and not fully clear. The deadline is "one month" (shown here as 30 days). Acts 2026, No. 63 added wording that lets the landlord send the itemized statement either within one month or within 15 days after that one-month date, so a landlord keeping part of the deposit may have roughly 45 days to explain the deductions; how courts will read this alongside the one-month refund rule is not yet settled. The law does not protect a tenant who abandons the unit without required notice or before the lease ends. The penalty requires willfulness, so send a written demand and allow 30 days. Attorney fees can go to whichever side wins.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who willfully fails to follow these rules can owe the amount wrongly kept plus $300 or twice the amount wrongly kept, whichever is greater. Failing to pay within 30 days of a written demand counts as willful. Please treat this letter as that demand

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends (for renters without a written lease: after the tenancy ends or the landlord accepts the unit back, whichever is later)
states.deadline_note: With a written lease, the deadline is whatever the lease says, up to 30 days. With no written lease (tenancy at will), it is 21 days. The landlord meets the deadline by mailing to your last known address.
states.itemization: A written statement itemizing the reasons for keeping any of the deposit, sent together with full payment of the rest.
states.penalty: A landlord who misses the deadline loses the right to keep any of the deposit. For wrongful withholding you can recover double the amount wrongly kept, plus reasonable attorney fees and court costs. You must first give the landlord at least 7 days' notice that you plan to sue; if the full deposit is not returned in those 7 days, the withholding is presumed wrongful.
states.source_quote: In the case of a written rental agreement, within the time, not to exceed 30 days, stated in the agreement; and ... In the case of a tenancy at will, within 21 days after the termination of the tenancy
states.flag: The deadline depends on your situation: up to 30 days as stated in a written lease, or 21 days if there is no written lease. These rules do not apply to a building with 5 or fewer units where the landlord lives in one of them. You must give 7 days' notice before suing.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who misses the deadline loses the right to keep any of the deposit, and a tenant can recover double the amount wrongly kept, plus reasonable attorney fees and court costs. Please treat this letter as my notice that I intend to sue if the deposit is not returned within 7 days

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: If you were evicted or left before the lease ended, the normal deadline does not apply: you must mail the landlord a written request with your new address within 45 days of leaving, and the landlord then has 45 days from receiving it.
states.itemization: If the landlord keeps any of the deposit, they must send by first-class mail to your last known address a written list of the damages claimed and an itemized statement of costs, with supporting documentation (an estimate is allowed if repairs are not finished). A landlord who does not send it loses the right to keep any of the deposit for damages.
states.penalty: If the landlord fails to return the deposit and interest within 45 days without a reasonable basis, you can sue for up to 3 times the amount withheld, plus reasonable attorney fees.
states.interest: Yes. Simple interest at the 1-year U.S. Treasury yield curve rate (as of the first business day of each year) or 1.5% a year, whichever is greater, on deposits of $50 or more that were held at least 6 months.
states.source_quote: Within 45 days after the end of the tenancy, the landlord shall return the security deposit to the tenant together with simple interest
states.flag: Tenants who were evicted or who abandoned the unit before the lease ended only get these protections if they send the landlord a written demand with their new address by first-class mail within 45 days of leaving. The up-to-3x penalty applies only when the landlord had no reasonable basis for withholding.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who keeps a deposit without a reasonable basis can owe up to three times the amount withheld, plus reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends (or, with no lease, after you move out)
states.deadline_note: The clock runs from the end date in a written lease, or from when you actually leave if you are a tenant-at-will.
states.itemization: For damage deductions, the landlord must give you within the 30 days an itemized list of damages sworn under penalty of perjury, describing the damage and repairs in detail, with written evidence of cost such as estimates, bills, invoices or receipts. A landlord who does not do this loses the right to keep any of the deposit.
states.penalty: If the landlord does not return the deposit (or the balance you are owed) with interest within 30 days, you are awarded 3 times that amount, plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney fees. The statute does not require bad faith.
states.interest: Yes, if the landlord holds the deposit for a year or longer: 5% a year, or the lower amount actually paid by the bank, paid to you each year and within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
states.source_quote: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof
states.flag: Massachusetts has many additional technical rules (separate bank account, receipts, condition statement, transfer on sale); a landlord who breaks some of them can lose the right to keep any deposit and owe triple damages even apart from the 30-day deadline.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not return the deposit, or the balance owed, with interest within 30 days owes three times that amount, plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out
states.deadline_note: You must give the landlord your forwarding address in writing within 4 days after moving out; if you do not, the landlord does not have to send the damage notice (though you can still claim the deposit). If the landlord misses the 30 days, the full deposit is due immediately.
states.itemization: The landlord must mail an itemized list of the damages claimed, with the estimated repair cost of each item and the basis for each charge, together with a check or money order for the rest of the deposit (or an electronic payment within 10 days after mailing the notice). The notice must warn you that you have 7 days to respond.
states.penalty: If the landlord keeps deposit money without following the required process (including going to court within 45 days when you dispute the charges), the landlord gives up all damage claims and owes you double the amount of the deposit kept.
states.source_quote: the landlord shall mail to the tenant, within 30 days after the termination of occupancy, a notice of damages that contains an itemized list of damages claimed
states.flag: Michigan has a special back-and-forth process. (1) Give your forwarding address in writing within 4 days of moving out. (2) The landlord has 30 days to mail an itemized damage notice. (3) You must reply by mail within 7 days of receiving it, saying in detail what you agree and disagree with, or you lose the amount claimed. (4) If you dispute it, the landlord must return the disputed money or sue within 45 days of move-out; otherwise the landlord owes double. Unpaid rent is treated differently and can be kept without a lawsuit. Section 554.609 was amended effective Sept. 21, 2026 (2026 PA 102) to allow electronic refunds.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who keeps deposit money without following the required process gives up all damage claims and owes double the amount of the deposit kept

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and the landlord has your mailing address or delivery instructions
states.deadline_note: The statute says "three weeks." The deadline is only 5 days if you had to leave because the building was condemned (and it was not your fault). Mailing by first-class mail within the deadline counts as on time.
states.itemization: The landlord must either return the deposit with interest or give you a written statement showing the specific reason for keeping any part of it. In court, the landlord has the burden of proving the reason for withholding.
states.penalty: If the landlord does not return the deposit or send the written statement in time, you can recover the amount wrongfully withheld plus an equal amount as a penalty (in effect double), with interest. Keeping the deposit in bad faith adds up to $500 in punitive damages; bad faith is presumed if the landlord missed the deadline.
states.interest: Yes. Simple interest at 1% a year, from the first day of the month after the deposit was fully paid (amounts under $1 are excluded).
states.source_quote: Every landlord shall: (1) within three weeks after termination of the tenancy; or (2) within five days of the date when the tenant leaves the building or dwelling due to the legal condemnation
states.flag: The deadline is stated as "three weeks" (21 days), and the clock depends on the landlord having your mailing address or delivery instructions. A shorter 5-day deadline applies after a condemnation. The same penalty also applies if the landlord skips the move-in/move-out inspection notice required by a separate section (504B.182).
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not return the deposit or send a written statement on time owes the amount wrongfully withheld plus an equal amount as a penalty, with interest, and can owe up to $500 more for acting in bad faith

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends, you give back possession, and you ask for the deposit
states.deadline_note: All three things must happen before the 45 days start: the tenancy ends, you hand back the unit, and you demand the deposit. Make the request in writing and keep a copy.
states.itemization: To keep any of the deposit, the landlord must deliver a written notice to you that itemizes the amounts claimed.
states.penalty: If the landlord keeps the deposit in violation of the law and not in good faith, you may recover up to $200 on top of your actual damages. There is no multiplier.
states.source_quote: shall be returned to the tenant no later than forty-five (45) days after the termination of his tenancy, the delivery of possession and demand by the tenant
states.flag: The 45 days only start once you ask for the deposit back, so ask in writing. We could not open the official state code online, so this was checked against the text of the law as reprinted in a 2024 bill on the Mississippi Legislature's site. Confirm it before relying on it.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who keeps a deposit in violation of the law and not in good faith can owe up to $200 on top of the tenant's actual damages

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: The landlord complies by mailing the list and any payment to your last known address, so make sure the landlord has your new address.
states.itemization: The landlord must either return the full deposit or give you a written itemized list of the damages the deposit is being kept for, along with the balance. If carpet cleaning is deducted under the lease, the landlord must also give you a receipt for the actual cost within 30 days.
states.penalty: If the landlord wrongfully withholds any of the deposit, you recover twice the amount wrongfully withheld as damages. The statute does not require bad faith.
states.interest: None required by state law (the statute says any interest earned on the deposit belongs to the landlord)
states.source_quote: Within thirty days after the date of termination of the tenancy, the landlord shall: (1) Return the full amount of the security deposit; or (2) Furnish to the tenant a written itemized list of the damages
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who wrongfully withholds any part of a deposit owes the tenant twice the amount wrongfully withheld

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends or you hand back the unit and the landlord accepts it, whichever comes first
states.deadline_note: If an inspection shows no damage, no cleaning needed, no unpaid rent, and you can show no unpaid utilities, the landlord must return the deposit within 10 days. Give the landlord your new address; otherwise it is sent to your last known address.
states.itemization: The landlord must give you a written list of any rent due and any damage and cleaning charges, along with payment of the rest of the deposit. A landlord who does not provide the list loses the right to keep any of the deposit for damage or cleaning.
states.penalty: You can sue for the amount wrongfully withheld. There is no multiplier, and the court may award attorney fees to whichever side wins.
states.source_quote: Each landlord, within 30 days subsequent to the termination of a tenancy or within 30 days subsequent to a surrender and acceptance of the leasehold premises, whichever occurs first, shall provide the departing tenant with a written list
states.flag: Two deadlines: 10 days when nothing is owed, 30 days when the landlord makes deductions. These deadlines do not apply if the landlord ended the lease for a tenant violation and has a pending court claim. Before charging for cleaning, the landlord generally must give written notice and 24 hours to do the cleaning yourself.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not provide the required written list loses the right to keep any of the deposit for damage or cleaning, and a tenant can sue for any amount wrongfully withheld

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: If you give no mailing address or instructions, the landlord mails the balance and itemization to your last known address. Nebraska courts have said you need to have asked for the deposit back before you can recover attorney fees, so make a written request.
states.itemization: The landlord must deliver or mail the balance of the deposit together with a written itemization of what was kept.
states.penalty: You can recover the money owed plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees. If the landlord's failure was willful and not in good faith, you can also recover one month's rent or 2 times the deposit, whichever is less.
states.source_quote: The balance, if any, and a written itemization shall be delivered or mailed to the tenant within fourteen days after the date of termination of the tenancy.
states.flag: The extra penalty requires willful, bad-faith conduct and is capped at the lesser of one month's rent or twice the deposit. Court decisions noted on the official statute page say a tenant must show the landlord did not comply with a demand for the deposit in order to recover attorney fees.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover the money owed plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees, and a landlord who acted willfully and not in good faith can owe an additional amount of one month's rent or twice the deposit, whichever is less

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: The landlord can hand it to you where rent is paid or mail it to your current address, or your last known address if the new one is unknown.
states.itemization: The landlord must give you an itemized written accounting of how the deposit was used and return whatever is left.
states.penalty: If the landlord does not return what is owed within 30 days, the landlord is liable for an amount equal to the entire deposit, plus an additional sum set by the court of up to the entire deposit again. The court weighs the landlord's good faith, the parties' conduct and the harm to you when setting the extra amount.
states.source_quote: return any remaining portion of the security deposit to the tenant no later than 30 days after the termination of the tenancy
states.flag: The penalty is not a simple multiplier: the base amount is the entire deposit, and a second amount up to the entire deposit is at the judge's discretion.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not return what is owed within 30 days is liable for the entire deposit, plus an additional amount set by the court of up to the entire deposit again

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: You must tell the landlord your new address when the tenancy ends; a landlord is not liable for missing the deadline if you did not. A deposit left unclaimed for 6 months after the tenancy ends becomes the landlord's.
states.itemization: The landlord must give you a written, itemized list of damages describing the repairs needed, with evidence that the repairs have been or will be done (such as receipts, estimates, bills or invoices). Deductions for unpaid rent, taxes or other charges must also be itemized in writing.
states.penalty: A landlord who does not comply owes twice the deposit plus interest due, minus any payments made and any amounts you legitimately owe for damage, unpaid rent or taxes. The statute does not require bad faith.
states.interest: Yes, if the landlord holds the deposit for a year or longer: interest at the rate paid on regular savings accounts at the New Hampshire bank where it is held.
states.source_quote: a landlord shall return a security deposit to a tenant and pay the interest due, if any, within 30 days from the termination of the tenancy
states.flag: These rules do not cover every landlord. Someone renting out a single-family home who owns no other rental property, or renting units in an owner-occupied building of 5 units or fewer, is not a "landlord" under this law (unless the tenant in that unit is 60 or older). You must also give your new address, and unclaimed deposits go to the landlord after 6 months.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not follow these rules owes twice the deposit plus any interest due, minus amounts legitimately owed

states.deadline_trigger: after your lease ends
states.deadline_note: Shorter deadlines apply in special cases: 5 business days if you are forced out by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, and 15 business days if the lease was ended early under the domestic-violence law. The landlord must return the money in person or by registered or certified mail.
states.itemization: The landlord must send an itemized list of any deductions and of the interest earned, delivered in person or by registered or certified mail.
states.penalty: If you sue and win, the court must award double the amount owed to you, plus court costs; attorney fees may be added at the judge's discretion. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.interest: Yes. The landlord must keep the deposit in an interest-bearing account (or money market fund) and pay you the interest, or credit it toward rent, every year; any unpaid interest comes back with the deposit.
states.source_quote: Within 30 days after the termination of the tenant's lease or licensee's agreement, the owner or lessee shall return by personal delivery, registered or certified mail the sum so deposited
states.flag: If you rent in a building the owner lives in that has no more than two rental units, these rules only apply after you give the landlord 30 days' written notice that you are invoking the security deposit law. We could not open the official state code online, so this was checked against a free copy of the 2025 code (Justia) instead. Confirm it before relying on it.
states.penalty_letter: a court must award a tenant who wins double the amount owed, plus court costs

states.deadline_trigger: after the rental agreement ends or you move out, whichever is later
states.deadline_note: The landlord meets the deadline by mailing the list and any payment to your last known address, so make sure they have a current address for you.
states.itemization: The landlord must give you an itemized written list of the deductions along with whatever balance is left.
states.penalty: A landlord who misses the 30-day deadline loses the right to keep any of the deposit, cannot countersue or sue you separately for damage, and owes your court costs and reasonable attorney fees. A landlord who keeps the deposit in bad faith also owes you a $250 civil penalty. There is no double or triple damages rule.
states.interest: Only if you have a one-year lease and the deposit is more than one month's rent; then the landlord must pay you interest every year at the passbook savings rate.
states.source_quote: the owner shall provide the resident with an itemized written list of the deductions from the deposit and the balance of the deposit, if any, within thirty days of the date of termination of the rental agreement
states.flag: We could not open the official state code online, so this was checked against a free copy of the 2025 code (Justia) instead. Confirm it before relying on it.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who misses the 30-day deadline loses the right to keep any of the deposit and owes the tenant's court costs and reasonable attorney fees, and a landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith owes a $250 penalty

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out
states.deadline_note: A landlord who misses the 14 days loses the right to keep any part of the deposit. The landlord must also offer you a walk-through inspection before you move out so you can fix problems first.
states.itemization: The landlord must give you an itemized statement explaining the reason for each amount kept, and return the rest.
states.penalty: You can recover your actual losses. If the landlord broke the rule willfully (on purpose), the court can add punitive damages of up to twice the amount of the deposit.
states.interest: In buildings with six or more apartments the landlord must keep the deposit in an interest-bearing bank account; you get the interest minus a 1% yearly administrative fee the landlord may keep. Smaller buildings are not required to use an interest-bearing account, but if they do, the same rule applies.
states.source_quote: Within fourteen days after the tenant has vacated the premises, the landlord shall provide the tenant with an itemized statement indicating the basis for the amount of the deposit retained, if any
states.flag: The 14-day rule does not cover every rental. The statute carves out rent-controlled apartments and certain senior, assisted-living and adult-care housing, and this section by its own terms does not apply to rent-stabilized apartments, which are handled under a separate section (§ 7-107) that we did not confirm contains a 14-day deadline. The up-to-double punitive damages require a willful violation and are capped by the size of the deposit, not the amount wrongly kept.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who misses the 14-day deadline loses the right to keep any part of the deposit, and a landlord who willfully breaks these rules can owe punitive damages of up to twice the deposit

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and you give possession back to the landlord
states.deadline_note: If the landlord cannot work out the full amount of the claim within 30 days, they must send an interim accounting by day 30 and a final accounting within 60 days. If the landlord does not have your address, they must hold any balance for you to collect for at least six months.
states.itemization: The landlord must itemize any damage in writing and mail or deliver it to you together with the balance of the deposit.
states.penalty: You can sue to get the deposit back and recover any losses the landlord's violation caused. If the landlord's violation was willful, they lose the right to keep any of the deposit and the court may award attorney fees. There is no double or triple damages rule.
states.source_quote: mail or deliver same to the tenant, together with the balance of the security deposit, no later than 30 days after termination of the tenancy and delivery of possession of the premises to the landlord
states.flag: The landlord can stretch the final accounting to 60 days by sending an interim accounting within the first 30 days.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who willfully fails to follow these rules loses the right to keep any of the deposit and may be ordered to pay the tenant's attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the lease ends and you give possession back to the landlord
states.deadline_note: The landlord sends the list and money to the last address you gave them, so provide a forwarding address.
states.itemization: The landlord must itemize anything kept from the deposit and deliver or mail it with a written notice stating the refund due to you or any amount you still owe.
states.penalty: The landlord is liable for three times the amount of any deposit money withheld without reasonable justification.
states.interest: Yes. The deposit must be kept in a federally insured interest-bearing account and the interest paid to you when the lease ends, unless you lived there less than nine months.
states.source_quote: Such itemization together with the amount due must be delivered or mailed to the lessee at the last address furnished lessor, along with a written notice within thirty days after termination of the lease
states.penalty_letter: a landlord is liable for three times the amount of any deposit withheld without reasonable justification

states.deadline_trigger: after the rental agreement ends and you give possession back to the landlord
states.deadline_note: You must give the landlord your forwarding or new address in writing. If you do not, you can still get your deposit back but lose the right to the extra damages and attorney fees.
states.itemization: The landlord must deliver a written notice that itemizes and identifies each deduction, together with the amount due to you.
states.penalty: You can recover the money owed to you plus an equal amount in damages (in effect double the amount wrongfully withheld), plus reasonable attorney fees. No bad faith needs to be shown, but you must have given a forwarding address in writing.
states.interest: Only on the part of the deposit above $50 or one month's rent (whichever is greater), at 5% a year, paid annually, and only if you stay six months or more.
states.source_quote: Any deduction from the security deposit shall be itemized and identified by the landlord in a written notice delivered to the tenant together with the amount due, within thirty days after termination of the rental agreement
states.flag: The double-damages remedy is only available if you gave the landlord a forwarding address in writing.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover the money wrongfully withheld plus an equal amount in damages, along with reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends, you give possession back, and you ask for the deposit in writing
states.deadline_note: The clock does not start until you make a written demand for the deposit. If you do not demand it in writing within six months after the tenancy ends, the landlord keeps the deposit.
states.itemization: The landlord must itemize deductions in a written statement, delivered to you in person or by mail with return receipt requested.
states.penalty: The statute lets you recover the deposit (and any prepaid rent owed) but sets no extra penalty or multiplier for a landlord who wrongly keeps it.
states.source_quote: the landlord shall return the balance of the security deposit without interest to the tenant within forty-five (45) days after the termination of tenancy, delivery of possession and written demand by the tenant
states.flag: Special procedure: you must demand the deposit in writing, and you lose it entirely if you do not do so within six months. Many websites still say 30 days; the official statute text (amended in 2015, confirmed on both the state courts site and the Legislature's Title 41 PDF) says 45 days. The 45-day wording is tied to cases where the landlord keeps part of the deposit; the statute states no separate deadline for a full refund.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover the deposit after making a written demand for it

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and you give possession back to the landlord
states.deadline_note: The same 31 days applies to prepaid rent and last month's rent deposits. The accounting and refund must be delivered in person or by first-class mail (or by email or electronic transfer only if you agreed to that in writing).
states.itemization: The landlord must give you a written accounting that states specifically the reason for each amount claimed, with separate accountings for the security deposit and for prepaid rent.
states.penalty: You can recover twice the amount that was withheld without a written accounting or withheld in bad faith.
states.source_quote: within 31 days after the tenancy terminates and the tenant delivers possession the landlord shall give to the tenant a written accounting that states specifically the basis or bases of the claim
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover twice the amount withheld without a written accounting or withheld in bad faith

states.deadline_trigger: after the lease ends or the landlord accepts the unit back, whichever comes first
states.deadline_note: You must give the landlord your new address in writing when the lease ends or you move out. If you do not, the landlord is released from the deadline and the penalties in this law.
states.itemization: The landlord must give you a written list of the damages they claim you are responsible for, along with payment of the rest of the deposit and any interest owed.
states.penalty: A landlord who does not send the written list within 30 days loses the right to keep any of the deposit or sue you for damage. A landlord who does not pay what is owed within 30 days is liable for double the amount by which the deposit (plus interest) exceeds the actual damage you caused. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.interest: Only after the deposit has been held more than two years. From then on, deposits over $100 kept in an interest-bearing escrow account earn interest that is paid to you each year, minus a 1% yearly fee the landlord may keep.
states.citation: 68 Pa. Stat. § 250.512 (Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951, § 512); interest at § 250.511b (§ 511.2)
states.source_quote: Every landlord shall within thirty days of termination of a lease or upon surrender and acceptance of the leasehold premises, whichever first occurs, provide a tenant with a written list of any damages to the leasehold premises
states.flag: You lose the protection of this law (the deadline, forfeiture and double damages) if you do not give the landlord your new address in writing when you leave.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not send a written list of damages within 30 days loses the right to keep any of the deposit, and a landlord who does not pay what is owed within 30 days is liable for double the amount wrongly kept

states.deadline_trigger: after the latest of: the tenancy ending, you giving possession back, or you giving the landlord a forwarding address
states.deadline_note: The 20 days does not start until you have given the landlord a forwarding address for the deposit.
states.itemization: The landlord must deliver a written notice itemizing any unpaid rent, reasonable cleaning or trash-removal costs, and damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, together with the amount due to you.
states.penalty: You can recover the amount owed to you plus damages equal to twice the amount wrongfully withheld, plus reasonable attorney fees. No bad faith needs to be shown.
states.source_quote: within twenty (20) days after the later of either termination of the tenancy, delivery of possession, or the tenant’s providing the landlord with a forwarding address for the purpose of receiving the security deposit
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover the amount owed plus damages equal to twice the amount wrongfully withheld, along with reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends, you hand back the unit, and you ask for the deposit back (whichever happens last)
states.deadline_note: The 30 days runs from the latest of three things: the tenancy ending, you giving back possession, and you demanding the deposit. Give the landlord a forwarding address in writing; without one you may lose the right to the extra damages.
states.itemization: The landlord must send a written notice itemizing every deduction, together with any money still owed to you.
states.penalty: Three times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus reasonable attorney fees, if the landlord does not return the deposit with the required notice. The statute does not require proof of bad faith.
states.source_quote: within thirty days after termination of the tenancy and delivery of possession and demand by the tenant, whichever is later
states.flag: The clock may not start until you actually ask for the deposit back, because the deadline runs from the tenant's demand if that comes last. Send a written demand with your forwarding address as soon as you move out.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not return the deposit with the required notice can owe three times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends and the landlord receives your mailing address or delivery instructions
states.deadline_note: The landlord must either return the deposit or send a written statement of the specific reason for keeping any of it within 21 days. If you ask, the landlord must also give a full itemized accounting within 45 days after the tenancy ends.
states.itemization: A written statement showing the specific reason for withholding. A detailed itemized accounting is only required if you request it, and is due within 45 days after the tenancy ends.
states.penalty: A landlord who does not comply loses the right to keep any of the deposit. If the landlord acted in bad faith, you can also get punitive damages of up to $200.
states.source_quote: shall, within twenty-one days after the termination of the tenancy and receipt of the tenant's mailing address or delivery instructions, return the security deposit
states.flag: This law was changed in 2026 (SL 2026, ch. 179): the deadline is now 21 days, not the two weeks that many older guides still show. The itemized accounting is only owed if you ask for it.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not follow these rules loses the right to keep any of the deposit, and a landlord who acts in bad faith can owe punitive damages of up to $200

states.deadline_trigger: no fixed statutory clock for returning the deposit
states.deadline_note: Tennessee's statute does not give a set number of days to return the deposit. It gives you a right to a move-out inspection and a written damage list, and limits the landlord to damage found within 30 days after you leave or 7 days after a new tenant moves in, whichever is earlier.
states.itemization: The landlord must inspect and make a full written list of damage with estimated repair costs; you have the right to attend the inspection and to sign or dispute the list in writing. A landlord who did not keep the deposit in a separate bank account and did not provide the damage list cannot keep any of it.
states.penalty: The deposit statute sets no multiplier or fixed penalty. A landlord who skipped the separate account and the damage list loses the right to keep any of the deposit, and you can sue in general sessions or circuit court.
states.source_quote: prior to the earlier of: (1) Thirty (30) days after the tenant vacated or abandoned the premises; or (2) Seven (7) days after a new tenant takes possession of the premises
states.flag: State law sets no fixed number of days to return a deposit. The 30 days often quoted is only the landlord's time limit for finding extra damage. This law is also commonly described as applying only in larger counties (over 75,000 people), which we could not confirm, so smaller counties may have no deposit law at all. We could not open the official state code online, so this was checked against a free copy of the 2025 code (Justia) instead. Confirm it before relying on it.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who did not keep the deposit in a separate account and provide the required damage list loses the right to keep any of it, and a tenant can sue to recover it

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out and surrender the unit
states.deadline_note: The landlord does not have to return the deposit or send the list until you give a forwarding address in writing, but you do not lose your right to the deposit by giving it late. A lease may require advance notice of move-out, but only if that clause is underlined or in bold.
states.itemization: If the landlord keeps any part, they must give you the balance with a written description and itemized list of all deductions. No list is required if you owe rent when you leave and the amount is not in dispute.
states.penalty: If the landlord keeps the deposit in bad faith: $100 plus three times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus attorney fees. A landlord who misses the 30-day deadline is presumed to have acted in bad faith, and one who in bad faith sends no itemized list loses the right to keep any of it.
states.source_quote: the landlord shall refund a security deposit to the tenant on or before the 30th day after the date the tenant surrenders the premises
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith is liable for $100 plus three times the amount wrongfully withheld, plus the tenant's reasonable attorney fees, and a landlord who misses the 30-day deadline is presumed to have acted in bad faith

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out and return possession to the landlord
states.deadline_note: If the landlord misses the 30 days, you must serve a written 'Tenant's Notice to Provide Deposit Disposition' in the form set out in the statute; the landlord then has 5 business days to comply. You cannot collect the penalty unless you serve that notice.
states.itemization: The balance of the deposit and any prepaid rent, plus a written notice that itemizes and explains the reason for each deduction. It can be mailed, delivered, or sent electronically if you gave the landlord a way to do so.
states.penalty: If the landlord still does not comply within 5 business days after your notice: the full deposit, the full prepaid rent, and a $100 penalty. Court costs and attorney fees go to the winner only if the other side acted in bad faith.
states.source_quote: No later than 30 days after the day on which a renter vacates and returns possession of a rental property to the owner or the owner's agent
states.flag: Special procedure: the penalty is only available after you serve the statutory notice and the landlord fails to respond within 5 business days. Section 57-17-3 was amended in 2025 (effective May 7, 2025).
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who does not comply within 5 business days of a tenant's written notice owes the full deposit, any prepaid rent, and a $100 penalty. Please treat this letter as that notice

states.deadline_trigger: after you move out (if you told the landlord the date) or after the landlord discovers you have left
states.deadline_note: For seasonal rentals that are not your primary home, the deadline is 60 days. The landlord complies by hand-delivering or mailing to your last known address.
states.itemization: A written statement itemizing any deductions, sent with the deposit.
states.penalty: A landlord who misses the 14 days loses the right to keep any of the deposit. If the failure was willful, the landlord owes double the amount wrongfully withheld plus attorney fees and costs.
states.interest: None required by state law. Towns may pass ordinances requiring interest, so check your local rules.
states.source_quote: A landlord shall return the security deposit along with a written statement itemizing any deductions to a tenant within 14 days
states.flag: Towns and cities can adopt their own deposit ordinances with extra protections (such as interest), so local rules may add to this.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who misses the 14-day deadline loses the right to keep any of the deposit, and a landlord who does so willfully owes double the amount wrongfully withheld plus attorney fees and costs

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends or you move out, whichever is later
states.deadline_note: If damage is more than the deposit and needs an outside contractor, the landlord can give written notice of that within the 45 days and gets 15 more days to itemize. If you give no forwarding address the landlord may hold the money in escrow, so provide one.
states.itemization: A written notice itemizing the deposit and all deductions, damages and charges, together with any amount owed to you. You also have a right to attend the move-out inspection and receive an itemized list of damages.
states.penalty: If the landlord willfully fails to comply, the court orders the deposit returned plus your actual damages and reasonable attorney fees (offset by any rent you owe). There is no multiplier.
states.source_quote: within 45 days after the termination date of the tenancy or the date the tenant vacates the dwelling unit, whichever occurs last
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who willfully fails to follow these rules can be ordered to return the deposit and pay the tenant's actual damages and reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the rental agreement ends and you move out (or after the landlord learns you abandoned the unit)
states.deadline_note: The landlord meets the deadline by handing it to you or mailing it first-class to your last known address within the 30 days.
states.itemization: A full and specific written statement of the reasons for keeping any of the deposit, with copies of estimates, invoices or receipts backing up damage charges. If the landlord's own staff did the work, the statement must show time spent and the hourly rate.
states.penalty: A landlord who misses the deadline owes the full deposit and generally cannot argue for any deductions in court. A court may award up to two times the deposit if the refusal was intentional, and the winning side gets court costs and attorney fees.
states.source_quote: Within 30 days after the termination of the rental agreement and vacation of the premises
states.flag: The up-to-double award is at the judge's discretion and requires an intentional refusal. Supporting documents are not required when money is kept for unpaid rent or charges other than damage.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who misses the deadline owes the full deposit, and a court may award up to twice the deposit for an intentional refusal, plus court costs and attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the tenancy ends
states.deadline_note: The deadline is 60 days after the tenancy ends or 45 days after a new tenant moves in, whichever is sooner. If damage is more than the deposit and needs an outside contractor, the landlord can give written notice within that time and gets 15 more days to itemize.
states.itemization: A written itemization of any damages or other charges deducted, delivered with the rest of the deposit in person or by mail to your last known or forwarding address.
states.penalty: If the landlord's failure is willful or not in good faith: the unreturned deposit plus damages equal to one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (offset by any rent you owe).
states.source_quote: "Notice period" means: (A) within 60 days of the termination of the tenancy; or (B) within 45 days of the occupation of the premise by a subsequent tenant, whichever time period is shorter.
states.flag: The deadline can be shorter than 60 days: it becomes 45 days after a new tenant moves in if that date comes first. The deadline itself is in the definitions section (§ 37-6A-1(7)), quoted from https://code.wvlegislature.gov/37-6A-1/.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who willfully or in bad faith fails to follow these rules owes the unreturned deposit plus damages of one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld

states.deadline_trigger: after your lease ends and you have moved out
states.deadline_note: If you leave or are evicted before the lease ends, the 21 days runs from the lease end date or the date a new tenant's tenancy begins, whichever is first. If you stay past the lease end, it runs from when the landlord learns you have left.
states.itemization: If anything is withheld, the landlord must deliver or mail a written statement describing each item of damage or other claim and the amount withheld for each, within the same 21 days.
states.penalty: Twice the amount of your financial loss, plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees. The statute does not require proof of bad faith.
states.citation: Wis. Stat. § 704.28(4); Wis. Admin. Code ATCP § 134.06; Wis. Stat. § 100.20(5)
states.source_quote: A landlord shall deliver or mail to a tenant the full amount of any security deposit paid by the tenant, less any amounts that may be withheld under subs. (1) and (2), within 21 days
states.flag: The itemized-list rule and the double-damages rule come from the state consumer-protection rule (Wis. Admin. Code ATCP 134.06) and Wis. Stat. § 100.20(5), not the deposit statute itself. The start date of the 21 days depends on whether you left on, before, or after the lease end date.
states.penalty_letter: a tenant can recover twice the amount of the financial loss, plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees

states.deadline_trigger: after the rental agreement ends, or 15 days after the landlord gets your new mailing address if that is later
states.deadline_note: The basic deadline is 30 days after the rental agreement ends or 15 days after the landlord receives your new address, whichever is later. If there is damage to the unit, the landlord gets 30 extra days (60 total). You must give the landlord your new address within 30 days of the end of the agreement.
states.itemization: The balance of the deposit and any prepaid rent, with a written itemization of deductions and the reasons for them, delivered or mailed to you.
states.penalty: If the landlord unreasonably fails to comply, you can recover the full deposit and court costs. There is no multiplier, and if you sue unreasonably and lose, you may have to pay the landlord's court costs.
states.interest: None required by state law (the statute says the deposit is returned without interest)
states.source_quote: within thirty (30) days after termination of the rental agreement or within fifteen (15) days after receipt of the renter's new mailing address, whichever is later.
states.flag: The 60-day figure applies only when there is damage to the unit; if the landlord is deducting only for things like unpaid rent, the 30-day deadline still applies. A separately identified utilities deposit follows different timing (refund within 10 days after you show the utility bills are paid). The lease must say if any part of the deposit is nonrefundable.
states.penalty_letter: a landlord who unreasonably fails to follow these rules can be ordered to pay the full deposit and court costs
